findings.title: JWT 'none' Algorithm Allowed — Signature Bypass
findings.description: The algorithms list now includes 'none', which allows an attacker to craft a token with no signature. Any client can forge an arbitrary JWT payload (e.g. admin role, any user ID) and it will pass validation. This is a well-known CVE class (CVE-2015-9235 pattern) and is trivially exploitable with no server access required.
findings.remediation: Remove 'none' from the algorithms list. The list should contain only the algorithm(s) your issuer actually uses, e.g. algorithms=['RS256'].

findings.title: Expiration Check Removed — Expired Tokens Accepted Forever
findings.description: The original code explicitly checked payload.get('exp', 0) < time.time() and rejected expired tokens. The new code removes this check entirely. Although PyJWT validates 'exp' by default when present, this change removes a defence-in-depth guard and, more critically, silently accepts tokens that contain no 'exp' claim at all — meaning tokens that were issued without an expiry (or with expiry stripped by an attacker) will now pass indefinitely.
findings.remediation: Restore the explicit expiry check, or ensure jwt.decode is called with options={'require': ['exp']} so tokens without an expiry claim are rejected. Do not rely solely on PyJWT defaults.

The security scan independently confirmed both as critical (CWE-347, CWE-613). The sole positive change — wrapping jwt.decode in a try/except to avoid an unhandled exception on malformed tokens — does not offset the regressions. issues.comment: algorithms=['RS256','none'] allows an attacker to present an unsigned token (alg=none, no signature) and pass validation. Remove 'none' unconditionally; the list must contain only the algorithm(s) your issuer signs with, e.g. algorithms=['RS256']. This is the CVE-2015-9235 / CWE-347 pattern and is trivially exploitable with zero server access.

The explicit expiry guard (payload.get('exp', 0) < time.time()) was removed. PyJWT validates 'exp' by default only when the claim is present; tokens issued without an 'exp' field, or tokens whose 'exp' was stripped by an attacker, now pass forever. Restore the check or add options={'require': ['exp']} to jwt.decode so missing-expiry tokens are hard-rejected (CWE-613).
